summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after developing rapid atrial fibrillation during dialysis, accompanied by shortness of breath, chest tightness, and fever. She was successfully rate-controlled with intravenous and oral metoprolol, converted to sinus rhythm, and found to have a subtherapeutic INR on admission, which was corrected with continued warfarin therapy. Evaluation for chest pain showed mildly elevated but stable troponins, attributed to chronic kidney disease rather than acute myocardial infarction. A viral upper respiratory infection was diagnosed after negative influenza testing, negative blood cultures, and chest imaging showing no pneumonia. Antibiotics were discontinued, and symptomatic treatment was provided. She completed two hemodialysis sessions during admission, remained stable, and was discharged home in normal sinus rhythm with updated medication instructions and follow-up plans.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
